speaker: EN_A
text: Welcome to KC desk note. Today we are unpacking one fresh research report and the question it raises.

speaker: EN_A
text: So, a new batch of clinical data just dropped for a drug called IBI363, and it’s getting a lot of attention. What’s the big picture here?

speaker: EN_B
text: Right. This is from a Nomura report on Innovent’s IBI363, which is a PD-1/IL2 bispecific. The early-stage data for non-small cell lung cancer, or NSCLC,

speaker: EN_B
text: looks quite promising, especially in two tough settings.

speaker: EN_A
text: Two settings—first-line treatment and IO-resistant. Which one is the real headline grabber?

speaker: EN_B
text: The IO-resistant late-stage NSCLC data is probably the most important. For patients who’ve already failed immunotherapy, the median overall survival was 18.

speaker: EN_B
text: 2 months, with a 24-month survival rate of nearly 48%.

speaker: EN_A
text: That sounds strong. How does that compare to what’s already out there?

speaker: EN_B
text: For context, a large trial called TROPPIN-Lung01 showed a median overall survival of just 9. 4 months in a similar population. So this is a meaningful step up,

speaker: EN_B
text: though we’re talking about a smaller patient group here.

speaker: EN_A
text: And what about the first-line setting, for patients who haven’t been treated yet?

speaker: EN_B
text: There, the most interesting result is from a sub-group that used a specific dosing schedule—3 mg per kg then dropping to 1. 5 mg per kg.

speaker: EN_B
text: That group showed an objective response rate of 86. 4%.

speaker: EN_A
text: That’s really high. But I imagine there’s a catch, or at least some caveats.

speaker: EN_B
text: Absolutely. First, both of these are based on relatively small patient cohorts, so we need larger trials to confirm. And second, safety is a key concern.

speaker: EN_B
text: In the IO-resistant group, over 99% of patients had treatment-related side effects, and nearly half were grade 3 or higher.

speaker: EN_A
text: So the efficacy signal is strong, but the safety profile is something to watch closely. What does the report say about the next steps?

speaker: EN_B
text: A global phase III trial for IO-resistant NSCLC is already ongoing, and we’ll see the clinical design at the upcoming ASCO meeting.

speaker: EN_B
text: There’s also a head-to-head trial comparing IBI363 with pembrolizumab and standard of care in first-line patients.

speaker: EN_A
text: That’s a lot of moving parts. But one thing I noticed—the report doesn’t fully settle the safety question, does it?

speaker: EN_B
text: No, it doesn’t. The safety profile is still a major open question, and the report flags it as a key risk.

speaker: EN_B
text: That’s one reason the full report is worth reading—it dives deeper into the trade-offs between efficacy and toxicity.

speaker: EN_A
text: So for listeners who want the full picture, what’s the one thing they should take away?

speaker: EN_B
text: IBI363 is shaping up as a potential first-in-class drug for a real unmet need, especially in IO-resistant lung cancer. But the safety story is far from written.

speaker: EN_B
text: If you want to understand the full risk-reward, the full report has the details.

speaker: EN_A
text: Good point. We’ll leave it there for now. Thanks for breaking it down.

speaker: EN_B
text: My pleasure. And for anyone following this space, the ASCO presentation will be a key event to watch.
